2609.05104.title: Compact Bellman-Grounded Cognitive Maps for Cost-Aware Navigation
2609.05104.paper_summary: Biological agents navigate familiar environments not by re-solving routes for each new goal, but by reusing a learned map built once and read off as goals change. Existing artificial cognitive-map models mimic this reuse, yet their guidance is not explicitly grounded in additive heterogeneous route costs. Furthermore, they often struggle with memory efficiency: representative state-indexed and high-rank spectral constructions incur substantial storage growth as the environment scales. We present BCM, which grounds a reusable cognitive map in local edge costs through a self-supervised Bellman-grounded objective and a compact coordinate encoding, supporting changing goal queries without per-goal retraining. On weighted grids of up to $N=1600$ nodes, BCM maintains full success and only a 5\% mean Gap relative to exact Dijkstra search, compared with about $45\%$ for a connectivity-based spectral baseline. Notably, as the graph size increases from $N=400$ to $N=3600$, its memory footprint grows sublinearly while maintaining competitive performance, making our method scalable to complex environments. Together, these results show that additive route costs can be written into a compact, reusable cognitive-map representation, bridging the gap between biological flexibility and optimal path planning.
2609.05104.paper_summary_zh: 生物體在熟悉的環境中導航，不是為每個新目標重新解決路徑，而是通過重用一次建立的學習地圖，隨著目標的變化而讀取。現有的人工認知地圖模型模仿這種重用，但它們的指導並未明確基於加性異質路徑成本。此外，它們在記憶效率方面經常面臨挑戰：代表性狀態索引和高階譜構造在環境擴展時會產生大量的存儲增長。我們提出了BCM，通過自我監督的Bellman基礎目標和緊湊的坐標編碼，將可重用的認知地圖基於局部邊緣成本，支持在不針對每個目標進行重新訓練的情況下改變目標查詢。在最多$N=1600$個節點的加權網格上，BCM保持了100%的成功率，並且相對於精確的Dijkstra搜索僅有5%的平均差距，而基於連通性的光譜基線約為45%。值得注意的是，隨著圖的大小從$N=400$增加到$N=3600$，其記憶佔用增長是次線性的，同時保持競爭性能，使我們的方法能夠擴展到複雜環境。綜合這些結果顯示，加性路徑成本可以寫入緊湊的、可重用的認知地圖表示中，彌合生物靈活性與最佳路徑規劃之間的差距。
